anomalies.observed: On the SkylabModule sheet the BBQ10KBD keyboard connector U1 has COL5 (pin 19) and ROW3 (pin 18) both tied to the same net label NET0018, which also appears on SKW92A U11 pin 17 (LAN_PORT4_RX-).
anomalies.expected: Each of the 5 columns and 7 rows of the keyboard matrix must be a separate net so the SKW92A can scan the matrix; a column and a row must never share a net.

evidence.quote: U1 BBQ10KBD: COL5 (pin 19) -> NET0018; ROW3 (pin 18) -> NET0018 (SkylabModule sheet)
netlist shows 5 column + 7 row lines wired directly to SKW92A GPIO pins (matrix scanned by the module itself, not via an onboard keyboard controller)

anomalies.impact: Column 5 and row 3 are shorted together, so the keyboard matrix cannot be scanned correctly; keys in column 5 and row 3 will produce ghost/incorrect key codes and the keyboard will not work as intended.

anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the USB_A connector J4 has D+ (pin 3) labeled NET0013 and D- (pin 2) labeled NET0017, while on the SkylabModule sheet the SKW92A U11 has USB- (pin 19) labeled NET0013 and USB+ (pin 18) labeled NET0017.
anomalies.expected: USB D+ must connect to the module's USB+ pin and D- to USB-, so the two data lines are not crossed.

evidence.quote: J4 USB_A: pin 3 (D+) -> NET0013, pin 2 (D-) -> NET0017 (EthernetAndPower sheet)
U11 SKW92A: pin 19 (USB-) -> NET0013, pin 18 (USB+) -> NET0017 (SkylabModule sheet)

anomalies.impact: The USB data pair is polarity-swapped, so USB data communication with the SKW92A will not work (USB power is unaffected).

parsed.summary: The schematic contains at least one clear connectivity deviation: the BBQ10KBD keyboard matrix has column 5 and row 3 shorted together on net NET0018, which would break matrix scanning. A second likely deviation is that the USB D+/D- pair appears crossed between connector J4 and the SKW92A USB pins.
